newsitem.title: THAILAND: TelecomAsia to launch two new services.
newsitem.headline: TelecomAsia to launch two new services.

text.p: TelecomAsia Corp Plc said on Monday it plans to launch two new revenue-generating services -- a personal cordless telephone (PCT) and a voice dialling system (VDS) -- next year.

Company vice-president Kitti Kerati-thamkul told Reuters in an interview the firm was also confident it would complete the installation of all 2.6 million fixed lines allotted to it in a government concession by the end of this month as scheduled.
Kitti declined to detail projected revenue expected from the new services.
The PCT, which would enable mobile conversations over a specified distance, would be launched around mid-1997 and the VDS some time in 1997, he added.

The PCT service will initially be offered to commercial and residential users over an area of about 700 sq km in the Bangkok area. By 2000 it is expected to cover all of the Bangkok area and the three neighbouring provinces of Nonthaburi, Samut Prakan and Pathum Thani.
Kitti said the PCT service would initially be supplied to 570,000 subscribers and would reach one million subscribers by 2000.

He said the VDS service was being developed now and would enable subscribers to insert preferred numbers into a memory bank in their telephones. They would then be able to dial the number by calling it up verbally.
"We hope to launch this service sometime in 1997 within Bangkok," Kitti said.
